statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-35611 (GHSA-h27x-rffw-24p4): in the addressable gem from 2.3.0 to before 2.9.0, URI templates that use the explode modifier, or several variables with the + or # operator, compile to regular expressions with catastrophic backtracking, so matching a crafted URI against such a template can exhaust CPU (a denial of service): https://github.com/sporkmonger/addressable/security/advisories/GHSA-h27x-rffw-24p4. addressable is a separate gem; Ruby does not bundle it. The matched addressable 2.8.5 comes from the development lockfile of the bundled rbs 3.4.0 gem, gems/rbs-3.4.0/Gemfile.lock, which pins addressable 2.8.5, a dependency of json-schema, among the gems rbs uses for its own development and tests; it is byte-identical to the Gemfile.lock in the rbs 3.4.0 gem on rubygems.org (https://rubygems.org/gems/rbs/versions/3.4.0). A lockfile only records versions: it installs no code, and Ruby does not read it when it loads rbs. We downloaded every package built from the ruby-3.3 source in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 288 package files across x86_64 and aarch64, each checked against its repository index checksum: ruby-3.3, ruby-3.3-libs, ruby-3.3-dev, ruby-3.3-doc, ruby-3.3-dbg and ruby-3.3-full, 3.3.10-r0 through the current 3.3.14-r4 (ruby-3.3-libs 3.3.11-r1 and ruby-3.3-full 3.3.11-r1 are published for aarch64 only), and the 18 gem packages ruby3.3-bundler to ruby3.3-typeprof, -r0 through -r4. We searched the name and contents of every file in them, including the files inside the cached gem archives and gzip-compressed files they carry, for the string addressable. No file name or directory contains it, so no build installs an addressable gem directory, gem specification or lib/addressable source. The only files whose contents contain it are rbs-3.4.0/Gemfile.lock in every ruby3.3-rbs build and two C header comments in ruby-3.3-dev (ruby/internal/gc.h and ruby/internal/xmalloc.h) that use the English word addressable. So the vulnerable template code is not present in any build of this owner.

A lockfile only records versions: it installs no code, and Ruby does not read it when it loads rbs. We downloaded every package built from the ruby-3.3 source in the DHI Debian repository for Debian 13, 320 packages: ruby-3.3 and ruby-3.3-dev, every published version from 3.3.11-0 through the current 3.3.14-0 (80 versions) on amd64 and arm64, each checked against its repository index SHA-256. We searched the name and contents of every file in them, including the files inside the cached gem archives and gzip-compressed files they carry, for the string addressable. No file name or directory contains it, so no build installs an addressable gem directory, gem specification or lib/addressable source. The only files whose contents contain it are rbs-3.4.0/Gemfile.lock in every ruby-3.3 package, the same Gemfile.lock inside the cached rbs-3.4.0.gem archive there (identical to the rubygems.org gem), and two C header comments in ruby-3.3-dev (ruby/internal/gc.h and ruby/internal/xmalloc.h) that use the English word addressable. So the vulnerable template code is not present in any build of this owner. Debian has not fixed its separate ruby-addressable package in trixie (no-DSA, minor issue: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-35611); that package is not part of this owner, and this decision rests on the absence of the code above, not on Debian's rating.
